description: The exact ДК 021:2015 (CPV) code allow-list for banking & payments has not been finalised. Codes observed in live tenders so far: 66110000-4 (банківські послуги, incl. acquiring, cash servicing, card accounts), 66170000-2 (обробка фінансових транзакцій, клірингові послуги), 32440000-9 (телеметричне та термінальне обладнання — used for self-service terminals), 72260000-5 (послуги, пов'язані з програмним забезпеченням). The seed's 30123400 was not observed in any real UA notice.

Much banking/payments demand is misclassified under generic CPV codes and is only findable by free-text title matching (e.g. 'термінал самообслуговування' filed under telemetry equipment, ATM purchases filed under office machinery).

Purchases below the reporting threshold and those made via the e-catalogue/price quotation are structurally under-represented in the classic tender search, yet ATM/terminal servicing contracts are often small and recurrent.

Prozorro's CDB covers public buyers only. Commercial banks that are not state-owned procure outside it; their tenders appear, if at all, in brokers' commercial-procurement sections (SmartTender, Zakupivli.Pro commercial) or nowhere.

Under martial law, defence and certain security-related procurement disclosure rules changed, and some buyer/supplier details may be withheld or delayed. The exact current disclosure regime for banking-adjacent purchases by security-sector buyers was not researched in this pass.

Several hosts recorded here (public-api.prozorro.gov.ua, audit-api.prozorro.gov.ua, bi.prozorro.org, bipro.prozorro.org, specifications.prozorro.org, spending.gov.ua) were established from search results, official index pages and live document URLs, but were not individually fetched in this pass.
About 6 of the 14 currently accredited Prozorro marketplaces are recorded by legal name only, without a confirmed domain or an assessment of their commercial/below-threshold offering.

The cell's core rationale — below-threshold and purely commercial (non-state) tenders that never reach the central portal — remains only partially mapped. Confirmed commercial streams exist on Zakupki.Prom, SmartTender and PlayTender, but their volume, buyer mix and banking share are unquantified.

No marketplace-level machine-readable API was identified in this pass; only IZI.TRADE's human-facing search documentation was found. The central Prozorro OpenData API was not assessed here (it belongs to another cell).

English-language surfaces of the operators (smarttender.biz/en, zakupki.prom.ua/en) were identified but not compared against their Ukrainian originals for completeness. Russian-language variants of key terms (закупки, тендеры, эквайринг) were not exercised at all.

No archive strategy identified for marketplaces that lose accreditation (the register's 'відключені' list) or that shut down, such as Zakupivli24. Their historical commercial listings are at risk of permanent loss.
No banking/payments CPV (ДК 021:2015) code set has been fixed for filtering across platforms, so keyword monitoring is currently ad hoc and will under- or over-collect.
Watchdog outputs in this cell are sector-agnostic; nothing found is scoped to banking, payments, POS/terminal, acquiring or cash-handling procurement.
DOZORRO's regional NGO network (the /ngo/ profile directory) was not enumerated because the domain is WAF-blocked to plain fetch.

Only one substantive academic strand (GTI/Fazekas, plus a CGD 2019 working paper on Ukrainian e-procurement) was reached; Ukrainian-language peer-reviewed procurement analytics (Vyshcha shkola journals, NaUKMA/KSE working papers) were not systematically searched.
No RSS/API endpoints confirmed for any watchdog source in this cell; all collection methods proposed are crawl-based.
The interface between watchdog flags and the State Audit Service / AMCU complaint outcomes was noted only indirectly (DOZORRO complaint-routing and 'penalties' articles).
No per-company newsroom URLs captured for the core PSP/acquirer set (Fondy, WayForPay, LiqPay, Portmone, EasyPay, Interkassa, Platon, 4bill, PROSTIR-linked providers).
The specific ДК021:2015 (CPV) codes under which validators, ticketing systems, parking terminals, self-service kiosks and payment-acceptance services are classified were not enumerated.

Municipal e-ticket coverage captured for Kyiv, Lviv, Kharkiv and Ivano-Frankivsk/Khmelnytskyi only. Dnipro, Odesa, Vinnytsia, Zaporizhzhia, Ternopil, Chernivtsi, Poltava, Zhytomyr and Rivne schemes are uncovered.
Local-newspaper and city-council-bulletin channels — the documented route for some e-ticket operator selections — have no identified aggregator.
No official state registry source captured for company identity resolution (EDR / data.gov.ua) — only a commercial mirror (ua-region).
E-money issuers and utility-billing aggregators as a distinct segment were not separately mapped; they were only reached via the NBU register in the abstract.
Card-personalisation, cash-in-transit and ATM outsourcing/servicing providers in Ukraine (e.g. cash-management operators, card bureaux) were not enumerated in this pass.
Ukrainian integrators announce wins on Facebook and LinkedIn faster and more explicitly than on their own websites, but social channels were not systematically enumerated.

International core/card-platform vendors present in Ukraine (Temenos, BPC/SmartVista, OpenWay Way4, Finastra, FIS, Euronet, ACI, Compass Plus) were not individually checked for Ukraine-tagged newsroom items.
Vendor conference/exhibition materials (e.g. Ukrainian banking-IT forums, NBU-adjacent fintech events) that list sponsors and case-study presentations were not covered.
Wartime effects — relocation, damaged-branch rebuild programmes, donor-funded equipment supply — were not probed as a driver of vendor announcements since 2022.

No page was fetched in this pass; all candidates rest on search-result evidence. Member-list URLs for UAFIC, AUB and UCBS remain to be located, and the EMA/NABU member pages' HTML structure is unknown.
Banks' own career pages (PrivatBank, Oschadbank, Ukrsibbank, Raiffeisen, PUMB, Ukreximbank, monobank/Universal) were not enumerated; many procurement roles are posted only there.

Processors and infrastructure operators (e.g. UPC — Ukrainian Processing Center, ProstoPay-type PSPs, NBU's PROSTIR national payment system community) and their partner/participant lists were not covered.

Russian-language variants of key terms (закупки, тендерный менеджер, ассоциация банков) were not searched, although a share of UA banking-sector job ads and archived association content still uses them.
Telegram channels and Facebook pages of the associations and of the payments trade press — a fast, high-signal announcement channel in Ukraine — were not scouted beyond a single Facebook hit.
Buyer EDRPOU codes were confirmed only for a few entities (Ukrposhta 21560045, Ukrenergo 00100227, ДОТ 44725823); Ukrzaliznytsia and the 24 oblast administrations were not enumerated.
No CPV code map yet for payment and cash infrastructure as bought under non-banking classifications (cash registers, POS terminals, ATMs, cash-handling machines, self-service kiosks, ticketing).
Sub-threshold purchases (below UAH 50,000) are neither planned nor published in the e-system at all; no source found that captures them.
Deferred-disclosure contracts (published 10 business days after signature, or up to 90 days after martial law ends for urgent defence needs) create a moving backlog not yet modelled.

Not yet explored: AMCU appeals body (Колегія АМКУ) decisions, NABU/SAPO case materials, and donor-side procurement rules (World Bank, EBRD, EU Ukraine Facility) which govern reconstruction purchases outside national rules.
Oschadbank procures under a head-office EDRPOU plus ~20 regional branch EDRPOUs; only five branch codes were enumerated in this pass (09305480, 09325703, 09331508, 09338500, 09322277).

Buyer-side supplier qualification terms — the thing this cell exists to capture — were only confirmed for PrivatBank, Ukreximbank, Ukrgasbank (documents) and Ukrposhta. Oschadbank and Sense Bank remain undocumented on their own domains.

Only ДП «ДІЯ» (43395033) was confirmed among Diia-adjacent state operators. Other candidate operators in the digital-state and payments-rail perimeter (e.g. Ministry of Digital Transformation itself, state registry/IT operators, and the forthcoming 'Укрпошта Банк' legal entity once licensed) were not enumerated.

No CPV code mapping was built for the in-scope hardware/software categories (ATMs, cash recyclers, POS terminals, card personalisation, core banking, cybersecurity). Only one CPV was observed incidentally (39130000-2, office furniture) plus 72250000-2 (systems support services).
This pass mapped where tenders are announced far better than where awards and executed contracts are published (contract registry, framework-agreement call-offs, amendments).

The buyer watchlist currently holds confirmed EDRPOU codes only for NBU (00032106) and the Banknote Printing and Minting Works (21575489). Other NBU-controlled entities (e.g. the cash-handling/collection and IT service subsidiaries) have not been enumerated.
No CPV code set has been established for the technology in scope (cash processing, sorting, minting, HSMs, card personalisation, payment-system software, certification services).
Central-bank purchases conducted outside Prozorro under statutory exemptions or wartime rules are not covered by any identified machine-readable source.
English-language coverage of this cell is thin — English searching surfaced only Prozorro/OCP/TI meta-material, no NBU tender content.
Purchases financed by IFIs/EU (Ukraine Facility) may follow donor procurement rules and appear on donor portals rather than, or in addition to, Prozorro.

Three of the eight named cell banks — Universal/monobank, A-Bank and Pivdenny — have no working direct source; only marketplace and registry proxies exist, and for monobank and A-Bank not even that was confirmed.

Bank-issuer coverage on the three commercial marketplaces was established only for the banks reached by name search; there was no systematic enumeration of which financial institutions are tenants on each platform.

Tender documentation — the layer holding technical specifications and qualification requirements — generally sits behind free but mandatory supplier registration on the marketplaces, and behind APS-TENDER for OTP.
Snowballing surfaced foreign-owned private banks outside the seed list — KredoBank (PKO BP), ProCredit Bank, Piraeus Bank MKB — that fit the cell's definition exactly.

Parent-group procurement policy was searched in English only; parent-language sources (Hungarian for OTP, French for BNP Paribas and Credit Agricole, Polish for PKO BP/KredoBank) were not systematically covered.

Several dated policy artefacts were identified but not retrieved in this pass: Raiffeisen's standard contractual terms (04/2024, 04/2025), Credit Agricole's procurement roadmap and mandatory clauses (06/2024, 05/2020), UkrSibbank's Suppliers' CSR Charter, and KredoBank's tender-participant ethics code.
Russian-jurisdiction procurement sites (rostender.info, zakupki.kontur.ru) and sell-side tender-guarantee product pages contaminate every 'bank + тендер' query.

Bilateral development finance institutions active in Ukraine's financial sector but outside the cell's named list were not covered: KfW/DEG, Proparco, FMO, SIDA, USDFC, JICA, Norfund, plus the Council of Europe Development Bank (CEB) which is a named party to the MDB harmonisation MoU.
This pass identified entry points but did not execute in-portal filtered searches (ECEPP country=Ukraine + sector=financial institutions; UNGM country=Ukraine; WB opportunities country=Ukraine).

No API or bulk-data endpoint was confirmed for ECEPP, UNGM, UNDP procurement notices or DREAM. Only TED, the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, SAM.gov and (by policy commitment) DREAM's OCDS publication are believed machine-readable.
No mechanism was established for linking a donor-side notice (lender portal) to the downstream Ukrainian tender in Prozorro for the same package.
Ukrainian-language coverage in this cell is concentrated on rules/commentary sources; no uk-language primary donor notice corpus was identified.
No archival/retrospective source was secured for expired donor notices, which usually disappear from lender portals after closing.

No enumerated list yet of Ukrainian banks/PSPs and their exact EU-registration name variants and transliterations (e.g. NBU / Natsionalnyi Bank Ukrainy, PrivatBank / АТ КБ ПриватБанк, Oschadbank, Ukrgasbank, UkrCard, EPS 'Prostir').
The CPV code set that best captures banking/payments/cash-handling contracts has not been fixed for this cell.

Below-threshold notices on national portals of EU member states implementing Ukraine assistance (notably Estonia, Lithuania, Poland, Germany/GIZ) were not surveyed, yet implementers such as the Estonian e-Governance Academy contract there.
UN system channels (UNGM, UNDP Ukraine) and World Bank procurement for Ukraine were outside the searches performed, though they are adjacent cross-border notice channels.
Retention and back-catalogue depth of TED for expired Ukraine-linked notices, and whether award notices remain retrievable years later, was not established.
Only two Ukrainian-language queries were run; Ukrainian coverage of EU-level channels is inherently thin but was not exhausted.
No EDRPOU-code list yet exists for banking-equipment vendors and integrators active in Ukraine, which is the join key across spending.gov.ua, Prozorro and Clarity Project.
CPV/ДК 021:2015 codes covering ATMs, POS terminals, cash-handling machines and their maintenance were not enumerated in this pass.

Local/municipal budget execution portals and communal enterprises (also E-data disposers) were not explored separately, though municipalities and communal utilities buy payment-acceptance infrastructure.
Martial-law era restrictions on publication of certain procurement and spending data were not assessed; some transactions and buyers may be hidden or delayed.
Opendatabot and YouContract/YouControl were referenced only indirectly; their contract and treasury-payment products were not evaluated.
No verified CPV (ДК 021:2015) code set for ATMs, POS/payment terminals, card personalisation, processing services, core banking and cash-handling equipment.
No named UA banking/payments vendor entities (with EDRPOU) were captured in this run — the supplier universe is still empty, only the machinery to build it was mapped.

Private-bank (non-state) procurement is largely out of Prozorro scope, so aggregator tender history covers state and state-bank buyers only; commercial-bank vendor relationships are invisible in this cell.
Sanctions and PEP registers (NAZK/NSDC sanctions lists) that these platforms also aggregate were not separately enumerated in this run.
No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed live; all entries rest on search-result evidence only.
The NABU official website URL (nabu.gov.ua) was inferred from the official Facebook handle rather than confirmed by a search result or fetch in this run.
Бюро економічної безпеки (BEB) and the Прокуратура/Офіс генерального прокурора were not searched as oversight channels for procurement-related economic crime in the banking sector.

Commercial-court (господарські суди) contract-dispute practice around supply/maintenance of ATMs, POS terminals and processing services was not searched with product-specific UA terms (банкомат, ПТКС, POS-термінал, процесинговий центр, еквайринг).
Licensing/ToS for automated collection from Opendatabot, Clarity Project and ZakonOnline was not established.
English-language coverage of this cell is thin by nature — AMCU/DASU/Accounting Chamber decisions are published in Ukrainian only; no English mirror of the appeals or monitoring corpora was found.
No confirmed dedicated API endpoint for DASU monitoring objects within the Prozorro API family was located in this run (only the general 2.5 tender API and the legal publication rule).
